rationale: polr1b knockdown reduces 47S pre-rRNA and kills neuroepithelial crest precursors by p53-dependent apoptosis; the subunit performs Pol I transcription/ribosome biogenesis, not a crest-specific step, so no crest process term is warranted (no crest-cell survival term exists in GO).
supporting_text: Hence, polr1b knockdown did not affect pol III function, but it specifically altered pol I activity and thus the generation of 47S pre-rRNA during ribosome biogenesis.

rationale: Abstract-only: Cnbp knockdown alters cranial crest apoptosis/proliferation balance and skeletogenic crest fate (a derivative-level fate, not crest identity); the general differentiation term with the acts_upstream qualifier is the most specific supported replacement.
supporting_text: demonstrate that Cnbp loss-of-function adversely affects the formation and survival of craniofacial cartilaginous structures not only controlling the ratio of cell proliferation and apoptosis but also defining skeletogenic neural crest cell fate

rationale: Morphant phenotype scored only at 34-36 hpf as reduced/disorganized fli1:GFP cranial crest segments; the authors cannot separate migration from arch patterning, so only the general differentiation term (acts_upstream) is supported.
supporting_text: These data lend support for the function of Chd7 in proper CNC development and patterning. Whether the defects reported here are due to aberrant CNC migration or improper pharyngeal arch patterning remains to be investigated.

rationale: IEP: Id2 expression in the outflow tract is lost after cardiac crest ablation, i.e. Id2 expression depends on crest presence; this places Id2 downstream of crest and is expression-only, not participation in crest formation.
supporting_text: This data suggests that the presence of neural crest is required for normal Id2 expression in both chick and Xenopus heart development

replacement_labels: neural plate border formation;positive regulation of neural crest cell fate specification
rationale: SNW1 acts upstream of BMP receptors to set a border-specific BMP activity domain; zebrafish morphants lose sox10/foxd3 crest and expand the neural plate, rescued by BMP2b at the border. Border formation plus positive regulation of specification fits a signalling modulator under acts_upstream.
supporting_text: Indeed, zygotic expression of the zebrafish BMP2b near or at the neural plate border is sufficient to rescue the loss of neural crest fate in SNW1 morphant embryos.

rationale: Consistent with the reviewed Xenopus SoxE genes (sox8, sox9-a, sox10: GO:0014036); in this paper Sox9 (non-SUMOylatable) induces crest precursors and Grg4 recruitment by SUMO-Sox9 represses crest markers.
supporting_text: SoxE proteins in which the SUMO acceptor site has been mutated to prevent SUMOylation are potent inducers of neural crest precursor cells, whereas SoxE factors with a SUMO moiety constitutively attached inhibit neural crest

replacement_labels: negative regulation of neural crest cell fate specification
rationale: Knockdown expands the expression domains of tfap2a, snai2 and foxd3 at 12 hpf (with elevated Hsf1 activity), i.e. hsbp1 restrains crest specifier expression; a negative regulation term fits the acts_upstream qualifier better than any participation term.
supporting_text: Knockdown of zebrafish HSBP1 leads to the expansion of the domain of cells expressing the NC inducers, tfap2a, snail2 and foxd3.

rationale: Gene-level consistency with the reviewed Xenopus SoxE genes (GO:0014036); this paper itself shows only that cis-regulatory deletions reduce or abolish embryonic sox10 expression and perturb adult pigment stripes, so the specification call rests on sox10's established role rather than this assay.
supporting_text: One hundred percent of sox10min homozygous mutants did not express any sox10 as compared to wild-type and heterozygous siblings
